t: For necessary expenses of the Aviation Advisory Commission, authorized by section 12 of the Act of May 21, 1970 (Public Law 91–258), $1,250,000, to be derived from the Airport and Airway Trust Fund and to remain available until March 1, 1972: Provided, That this appropriation shall be available to reimburse the “Emergency fund for the President” for allocations made for the purposes of this appropriation.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the words "Aviation Advisory Commission" signal an advisory body with outside members, which would be participation. But this section only appropriates money for the Commission's expenses; the Commission was established and its membership and duties set by a different statute (section 12 of Public Law 91-258). Nothing in this text itself creates the body, defines non-federal membership, or requires consultation, comment, or a hearing before a federal decision. The call is uncertain because funding an advisory commission could be read as supporting participation.
fable.s: For necessary expenses of the Aviation Advisory Commission, authorized by section 12 of the Act of May 21, 1970 (Public Law 91–258), $1,250,000, to be derived from the Airport and Airway Trust Fund

opus.w: The section funds the operations of an advisory commission whose role is to advise federal aviation policy. I believe the statute that created it called for members drawn from outside government. Under the examples, an advisory body counts as participation even when its members aren't listed, so supporting its work leans Yes. The opposite reading has some force: this is only an appropriation, like Example 1, and it creates no new process. That is why my confidence is moderate.
opus.s: For necessary expenses of the Aviation Advisory Commission, authorized by section 12 of the Act of May 21, 1970 (Public Law 91–258), $1,250,000
opus.b:
I labelled this **Yes**, with only moderate confidence.

1. **The tempting reading and why it falls short.** This looks like a plain appropriation, and Example 1 marks a funding provision "No". But this money goes only to an advisory commission whose job is to advise federal aviation decisions, so funding it keeps that advisory process running.
2. **Who is involved.** The section doesn't say who sits on the Commission. From background knowledge (not from the section), I believe the 1970 statute that created it had the President appoint members from outside government, including people from the aviation field. Examples 8, 10 and 12 count an advisory body as participation even when its members aren't spelled out.
3. **Uncertainty.** The section itself creates no new process. It only funds an existing commission, so a "No" label could reasonably be defended.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriation provision that authorizes funding for the Aviation Advisory Commission. It does not describe the composition of the commission, its advisory role, or any requirement for the federal government to consult with outside parties. Merely funding a commission does not constitute participation as defined, especially without evidence that the commission includes non-federal members or that its advice is sought from outside the government.
qwen_chat.s: For necessary expenses of the Aviation Advisory Commission, authorized by section 12 of the Act of May 21, 1970 (Public Law 91–258), $1,250,000, to be derived from the Airport and Airway Trust Fund and to remain available until March 1, 1972
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: The text mentions an "Aviation Advisory Commission," which sounds like an advisory body that might involve outside experts or public participation.
Resolution: The section is purely an appropriation clause providing funds for the commission's expenses. It does not describe the commission's membership, its duties, or any process of consultation with outside parties. The existence of a commission is not sufficient to label this section as requiring participation unless the section itself mandates interaction with non-federal entities. Here, it only authorizes spending.
